text:
maya: Heads-up — customer ACME Corp (tenant acme-prod) reports spike of 502s from hosted API during large embed batch jobs starting ~08:10 UTC.
sam: Got ticket? any repro payloads or trace ids?
maya: Ticket #T-8832, they sent a curl repro in the ticket. Sawtooth pattern: bursts every ~30s for ~3m then quiet.
anne: Escalating. Can someone grab ingress traces + envoy logs for that time window? cc @lia
lia: Pulling traces now. I see many upstream resets to upstream svc edge-upstream-01 and 5xx at envoy level. Sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d
jake: Also seeing connection window saturation on the gateway at the same times, h2 stream quota exhaustion in a few hosts.
eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot: Deployed frontend-auth-cache tweak at 07:58 UTC to eu-west1 (rollout 5/5) — no rollback.
maya: Hmm deploy around 07:58 could align with first alerts, but bursts start 08:10.
sam: Can you paste the customer's curl (sanitized) and headers they used? we need to check large metadata + billing headers.
maya: From ticket (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-prod" \ 
  -H "X-Billing-Token: <redacted>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","inputs":["<very long document...>"],"batch_size":256}'

lia: Large batch_size + huge single doc, plus custom billing header — that can cause backend fanout + larger upstream multiplexing. Could push upstream connpool limits.
jake: Confirmed: auth-proxy opened ~250 concurrent streams for that tenant on some frontdoor hosts. Some frontdoors hit max concurrent streams and returned 502s when upstream couldn't accept.
anne: Customer impact high — they're in prod. What's immediate mitigation? Can we throttle or reject large batch_size server-side?
sam: Quick mitigation: add short-term rate-limit rule for X-Tenant-ID acme-prod at edge (15s window, soft limit) and force the proxy to downgrade batch_size for that tenant using request rewrite.
lia: I can push a temporary rate-limit and a rewrite to cap batch_size to 32 for acme-prod. Will test on a single canary host first.
maya: Please do canary to 2 hosts in eu-west1, notify support before roll.
eng-sre-bot: ops-runbook: Applied temporary iptables conn limit on frontdoor-03 as an emergency throttling — check logs.
jake: After throttling, error rate dropped to baseline in 2m on canary hosts. But global load still shows a few hot hosts.
sam: Follow-up fixes: 1) increase frontdoor per-tenant stream quota and connection pool sizing 2) auth-proxy behavior: reject >128 streams per tenant instead of letting upstream fail 3) implement batch_size server-side safety limits.
lia: I'll open PR for server-side cap and feature flag for tenant-specific batch overrides. Short-term config change for pool sizing requires infra review.
anne: Communicate to customer: apologize, explain temporary throttle and ask them to retry. Offer workaround: lower batch_size client-side to 64 until resolved. I'll draft message.
maya: Customer replied: "Thx, we can throttle on our side but need root cause. We'll hold bursts for now." They want ETA for permanent fix.
sam: ETA: config + infra changes ~48-72h, server-side batch cap PR deployable in ~24h behind flag. I'll own rollout plan.
jake: Action items I/O: collect full envoy logs for affected hosts (saved to s3://redwood-support/esc-T8832/), add postmortem stub, schedule infra tweak window.
lia: Repro steps documented:
1) Use curl above with model embed-large-v2
2) send 8 concurrent requests with batch_size 256
3) observe 502s at gateway when sustained >200 concurrent streams from same tenant

Sample error snippet from envoy logs:
```
[2026-03-15T08:11:22Z] "POST /v1/embeddings" 502 NR upstream_reset_before_response: reset reason=remote_reset stream_id=45 tenant=acme-prod trace=trace-0a1b2c3d
```

sam: Good. Add note to disable the 07:58 deploy tweak if we can confirm correlation — but don't rollback without clear causation.
maya: For now I'll send customer a status update and offer a Credits concession. Anne can confirm wording.
anne: Draft sent and approved. Also scheduling postmortem with eng-sre + infra tomorrow. Marking thread for incident review.

maya: TL;DR: Cause = tenant burst + large batch_size + pool exhaustion at gateway; mitigation = temporary tenant throttle + canary batch cap; next = infra scaling + server-side safety limits.
